title: Lambros D. Callimahos
name: Lambros D. Callimahos
summary: U.S. Army and NSA cryptologist, teacher, and author who developed advanced cryptanalysis instruction including the CA-400 course.
whyThisMatters: Callimahos helped transmit cryptanalytic practice across generations of analysts. His teaching, writing, and course design made methodology—not only individual discoveries—a lasting part of security history.

sections.overview:
Lambros Demetrios Callimahos was a U.S. Army and NSA cryptologist, teacher, writer, and musician. He entered cryptologic service in 1941 and later worked with William F. Friedman.

Teaching cryptanalysis

At NSA he developed the advanced CA-400 cryptanalysis course, taught it repeatedly, and helped shape the Dundee Society formed by its graduates. The program emphasized analytical technique and disciplined practice.

Writing and institutional work

Callimahos wrote and revised cryptanalytic texts, including work associated with Military Cryptanalytics, and helped establish the NSA Technical Journal in 1955.

In memoriam

Callimahos died in 1977. His teaching legacy continues to be documented in NSA historical records.

timeline.event: Joins the U.S. Army and enters cryptologic service.
Serves in the China-Burma-India theater and later assists William F. Friedman.
Develops and teaches CA-400 at NSA.
Dies after retiring the previous year.
